title: Paffett wins Lausitzring Race 2 as pole-sitter Eng fades
dek: Gary Paffett won Race 2 at the Lausitzring for Mercedes from third on the grid, 1.427 seconds ahead of Marco Wittmann, after Philipp Eng lost the lead he took from his first DTM pole.

chapters.title: A weekend turned upside down on Saturday
text: Saturday’s Race 1 had been a chaotic affair. Edoardo Mortara won the shortened race from seventh on the grid, Timo Glock and Philipp Eng completed the podium, and Audi lost four cars in two accidents and left without a point. Glock led the standings on 62 points from Gary Paffett on 45.

Sunday began with more bad news for the Ingolstadt marque. René Rast, who had rolled his Audi on Saturday, was not cleared to race by the doctors, and Audi did not nominate a replacement. Race 2 would start with only 17 cars, five of them Audis.

chapters.title: Eng takes a first pole from Wehrlein by 0.026s
text: Qualifying was held in conditions that suited fast laps, with a warm track and cool air. Pascal Wehrlein opened with the first real marker of 1m38.226s, but Eng, fresh from his first DTM podium, took provisional pole from him at the end of the first runs. In the closing minutes Wehrlein and Paffett were the first to leave their garages for a final attack, yet Eng’s first lap held.

Eng’s 1m38.150s gave him the first pole position of his DTM career, 0.026 seconds clear of Wehrlein. Paffett was third, 0.068s off, and Marco Wittmann fourth, 0.133s behind despite the best first sector of anyone. Lucas Auer’s Saturday pole time of 1m37.343s was not threatened.

Rockenfeller was fifth, the only Audi in the top ten, and Mortara, who had been last after the first runs, improved to sixth. Joel Eriksson was seventh, Auer eighth, Daniel Juncadella ninth and Glock tenth, the championship leader reporting balance shifts in the first sector that cost him a great deal of time. Rast sat out the session.

chapters.title: Paffett and Wittmann pick off the pole-sitter
text: Unlike on Saturday, the start passed without incident, and Eng led into the first corner from Wehrlein, Paffett, Wittmann and Rockenfeller. On lap two Wehrlein used DRS to draw alongside Eng, but the Austrian held the place, and in the process Wehrlein lost second to his team-mate Paffett.

Within four laps Paffett had the lead from Wehrlein and Eng. The BMW rookie, who had no DRS of his own while being passed, was handed back place after place and fell to seventh at the flag. Eng later said that he had also run too wide at Turn 9 at one point, costing him two places. Wittmann went by the pole-sitter early, and by the middle of the race he had settled behind Wehrlein, closing on the Mercedes pair.

chapters.title: Wittmann stays out and jumps Wehrlein
text: The mandatory stops reshuffled the order. Jamie Green, among the last cars on the grid, came in at the end of the first lap and then ran the rest of the race on that one set of tyres, a gamble that carried him as high as sixth and made him the best Audi. Glock stopped on lap 15, dropped back and then had to fight his way up again from tenth on the grid.

At the front, Wittmann stayed out one lap longer than Wehrlein and came out ahead of him, taking second place on the road. Paul di Resta, who had started 15th, made the most of the stops to climb to fourth. Behind them, the midfield was a tangle of tyre-saving and DRS management, with Rockenfeller, Auer and Juncadella scrapping over the last points places.

chapters.title: Paffett holds Wittmann off by 1.427 seconds
text: Paffett had a comfortable cushion after the stops, but Wittmann was faster in the second half of the race and took a tenth or two out of the gap on most laps, setting the fastest lap of the race on lap 17. Paffett switched from tyre-saving to flat-out driving, made a few small errors and ran wide at times, but never quite lost touch with the front. Wittmann could not reach the DRS window he needed.

Paffett took the flag after 34 laps in 57:27.909, 1.427 seconds ahead of Wittmann. Wehrlein was third, 8.602s behind, ahead of di Resta, Glock and Green. Eng, Rockenfeller and Eriksson completed the top nine, and Robin Frijns picked up the last point in tenth, his first of the season, after working his way past the midfield group late in the race.

chapters.title: Paffett within a point of Glock as Mercedes celebrates
text: Paffett said the pulse had not been as high as at Hockenheim but still high at the end. He called it a hot, difficult race in which the car slid a lot and staying in front was hard work, and he explained that once Wittmann started to close he had to stop managing his tyres and drive flat out for around a dozen laps. It was a second win of the season, after the one at Hockenheim, and he said that after a Saturday that had not gone to plan, the team had answered on Sunday with another win in a weekend.

Wittmann, who had started fourth, was delighted with second place. He said he had tried hard to get into Paffett’s DRS window but ran out of laps, and that the result felt almost like a win. It was his first podium of the year. Wehrlein was pleased to be on the podium for the first time since returning to the DTM, although he felt the two cars ahead had managed their tyres a little better, and Mercedes team principal Ulrich Fritz praised a great weekend for the whole team. For Mercedes it was a third win in the first four races of the season, against one for BMW.

The championship was suddenly tight. Glock, who recovered from tenth on the grid to fifth, kept the lead on 72 points, but Paffett, with 71, was only one point behind. Glock said that rivals on aggressive strategies had got ahead of him and that he had lost a lot of DRS early on, though he was content with fifth. Audi’s motorsport chief Dieter Gass said it had been a bad weekend, with the Saturday accidents expensive and a lack of performance still obvious, and that Green’s sixth place on a risky strategy was a good drive. Green said the new regulations did not suit Audi, and Frijns had at least scored his first points.

BMW took some comfort from three podiums over the two races, with Glock and Eng on the Saturday podium and Wittmann on Sunday’s, and BMW’s motorsport director Jens Marquardt noted that the Berlin Formula E race had been held on the same weekend, only 140 kilometres away. BMW Motorsport’s vehicle development chief Rudolf Dittrich said the changes to the track layout had paid off with better racing, and that the manufacturer had put five cars in the top ten on Saturday and four on Sunday. The next round was two weeks later at the Hungaroring.

facts.t: Paffett’s second win of the year
facts.v: Gary Paffett won Race 2 in 57:27.909 over 34 laps, 1.427 seconds ahead of Marco Wittmann, after starting third.
